title: Curse
wikitext:
'''Curses''' are a category of [[debuff]], most of which can be applied by player [[skill]]s. Curses are split into two categories: '''Hexes''' and [[Mark]]s.

==Mechanics==
Curses are a type of debuff. Each curse debuff has default values, visible in the reminder text of stats which apply the curse. When applied by a ''skill'', the skill overrides these default values. In general, curses are balanced so that a level 1 curse skill without quality applies the curse with the default values, and higher levels override them with higher values.<ref>https://www.reddit.com/r/pathofexile/comments/jmbhl4/default_level_of_curses_if_item_has_curses_enemy/gaubbpf/</ref>

Curses from the player are removed when the player dies, leaves the area, or loses the cursing skill (e.g. by swapping weapons). Non-skill curses inflicted by the player's [[proxies]] are removed when the proxy dies; curses from skills are not. Dead entities cannot inflict curses. 

[[Monster]]s and [[map]]s can have [[modifier]]s that make them (or monsters inside of them, in the case of maps) [[hexproof]] or [[Curse immunity|immune to curses]].

Curses are split into two categories: '''Hexes''' and '''Marks'''.

===Hexes===
Hexes are spells which apply the curse in an [[area of effect]]. Note that the term "Hex" by itself refers specifically to Hex Curse skills. {{il|Bane}} and {{il|Hexblast}} have the Hex gem tag, but they are not Hex Curse skills.

Hexes can be turned into an [[aura]] by linking it with either {{il|Blasphemy Support}} or {{il|Awakened Blasphemy Support}}.

Hexes can appear as modifiers on [[equipment]] and [[map]]s, which apply the default curse debuff to the specified target. 

Hexes can be applied to monsters or players with [[Hexproof]], causing them to be considered cursed, but will be unaffected by any debuffing stats unless the user can bypass Hexproof (e.g. via {{psl|Unholy Authority}} or {{il|Cospri's Will}}). Hexes cannot be applied to targets that are Immune to Curses.

===Marks===
{{main|Mark}}
Marks are spells which apply a curse to a single target. Marks do not have a duration and will apply permanently on a target within a certain distance until removed or moved to another target. Marks are removed when the entity that inflicted the Mark is killed. 

An entity can only mark one target at any time. Applying a mark to a new target will cause the mark on the previous target to be removed. Marks cannot stack and a target can only be affected by a single mark at once, even with additional curse limits.

Hexproof does not interact with marks in any way. Marks cannot be applied to targets that are Immune to Curses.

===Curse effect=== 

{{Stat total|Curse Effect}}

'''Note:''' curse effect specific for a single curse, such as {{c|mod|% increased Frostbite Curse Effect}}, only applies to the corresponding curse ''skill gem'', not to non-skill curse modifiers like {{c|mod|Curse Enemies with Frostbite on Hit}}.<ref name="CurseEff"/>

===Curse limit===
By default, one curse can be active at a time on a creature. While a curse is active, applying a different curse on the same creature will expire the oldest curse, regardless of curse type or strength.<ref name="CurseEff"/> 

Hexes can be applied to different enemies, and different hexes can be applied to the same enemy through {{c|mod|You can apply an additional Curse}}. Mark curses, however, can only apply to one target at a time. For example, with +1 curse limit, you can have two Hexes or a Hex and a Mark on one target, but not two Marks.

When the curse limit is zero, casting a curse skill will not apply a curse, and targeted enemies are not considered "cursed" even for a moment.

Your curse limit can be increased with the following:
* {{psl|Whispers of Doom}}
* [[Occultist]]'s {{psl|Unholy Authority}} or [[Ascendant]]'s {{psl|id=AscendancyAscendant37}}
* {{il|Cospri's Will}} or a [[influenced item|Hunter-influenced]] body armour with mod: {{ml|AdditionalCurseOnEnemiesInfluence1|display=verbose}} or a body armour with Delve drop-only prefix {{ml|AdditionalCurseOnEnemiesDelve}}
* {{il|Doedre's Damning}} or a [[Precursor's Emblem]] with {{c|mod|You can apply an additional Curse while at maximum [[Power Charge]]s}}
* {{il|Windscream}}
* {{il|Vixen's Entrapment}}
* {{il|Sublime Vision}} with {{c|mod|You can apply an additional Curse while affected by Malevolence}}
* An amulet with the {{c|mod|You can apply an additional Curse}} [[corrupted]] implicit

This allows for a theoretical maximum of ten curses on an enemy at one time. The following items interact with your curse limit in other ways:

* {{il|Replica Doedre's Damning}} reduces your curse limit by one, to a minimum of zero.
* {{il|Doedre's Skin}} grants {{sl|id=SummonDoedresEffigy }}, effectively a Blasphemy Totem with its own +5 curse limit.
* {{il|Sentari's Answer}} applies hexes on [[block]] which ignore the curse limit.
* {{il|Ylfeban's Trickery}} applies hexes on getting hit which ignore the curse limit.
* {{il|Anathema}} sets your curse limit to your maximum {{stl|Power Charge}}s, overriding all other modifiers.

In addition, {{il|Self-Flagellation}} increases the maximum number of curses you can have on yourself.

===Curse priority===
There are a few rules when it comes to the interaction between multiple curses.

* Each player (or [[minion]]/[[mercenary]]) has their own curse limit. When an entity applies a curse, their highest limit is used first. For example, when entity A has a curse limit of 3, and applies 2 curses, those curses will be added to 'slots' #3 and #2 on the target. Entity B with a curse limit of 1 can apply a curse in slot #1 without conflict. These two entities will not remove each other's curses, regardless of application order.<ref>https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mcyjl3iMQ6I</ref>
* Curse auras (Blasphemy) override "on Hit" curse modifiers or cast/triggered curse skills. If your curse limit is full with Blasphemy, a self-cast curse will never apply on the enemy while in the Blasphemy's AOE (e.g. cannot proc {{il|Impending Doom Support}})<!-- tested by Lothrik/blvcksvn -->
** Multiple {{il|Blasphemy Support|Blasphemy}} Curses will take priority based on which Blasphemy was cast most recently with earlier ones getting replaced.<!--tested by Lothrik-->
*** {{il|Witchfire Brew}} and other curse auras function identically to Blasphemy, and follow the same rules of replacement.<!--tested in 3.24 by Jasmine-->
* Curse skills socketed in {{il|Mark of Submission}} will apply before triggered skills and non-skill curse on hit effects. 
* Triggered curse ''skills'' apply after Mark of Submission, but before non-skill on-hit curses. 
** If multiple curse skills trigger, they apply in this order: Main Hand ⇒ Amulet ⇒ Helmet ⇒ Off-Hand ⇒ Body Armour ⇒ Belt ⇒ Gloves ⇒ Boots ⇒ Ring 1 ⇒ Ring 2 with the earlier one getting replaced. <!--tested by Lothrik/blvcksvn--> This includes skills granted by items, such as {{il|Oskarm}}'s Assassin's Mark.<!--tested by Yohsene, 3.21--> 
*** Multiple curse skills from the same item trigger according to the [[Trigger#Order|trigger order]].<!-- tested by Lothrik -->
* Non-skill curse on hit modifiers apply after triggered skills. 
**If multiple non-skill curse debuffs are applied by the same hit, they are applied in this order: {{il|Temporal Chains}} ⇒ {{il|Enfeeble}} ⇒ {{il|Vulnerability}} ⇒ {{il|Elemental Weakness}} ⇒ {{il|Flammability}} ⇒ {{il|Frostbite}} ⇒ {{il|Conductivity}} ⇒ {{il|Despair}} ⇒ {{il|Punishment}} with the earlier one getting replaced.<!--tested by Lothrik--> Which gear slot the curse modifiers are granted by does not matter.<!--tested by Yohsene, 3.21-->
* [[Mark]] skills will always replace each other.

===Curses as map mods===
{{see also|List of map suffix mods}}

There are several [[map]] suffixes that cause players to be affected be a certain curse. They do not count against your curse limit, so you can be affected by one or more curses in addition to them, although they do not stack with the same curse applied by monsters. [[Minion]]s are unaffected by these curses. They affect the entire [[area]] and cannot be permanently removed, although immunity to curses will suppress them while it's active. 
The debuffs applied are not skills, but have values equivalent to curses from a level 1 skill gem.

{{Modifier table
|type=map
|q_tables=mod_stats, mod_spawn_weights
|q_join=mods._pageName=mod_stats._pageName, mods._pageName=mod_spawn_weights._pageName 
|q_where=mods.domain=5 
 AND mods.id LIKE "%Curse%" 
 AND mod_stats.id LIKE "%map_player_has_level_X%"
 AND mod_spawn_weights.value > 0
 AND (
     mod_spawn_weights.tag="low_tier_map"
  OR mod_spawn_weights.tag="mid_tier_map"
  OR mod_spawn_weights.tag="top_tier_map"
)
|stat_text=1
|spawn_weights=1
}}

===Curse immunity===
Currently, player can gain [[curse immunity]] in the following ways:

* {{stl|Consecrated Ground}} created around {{il|Holy Flame Totem}} 
* {{il|Kiara's Determination}}
* {{il|Chains of Emancipation}} (while having at least 25 [[Rage]])
* {{il|Witchbane}} (after killing an enemy affected by a non-aura [[Hex]])
* {{il|The Balance of Terror}} (after casting {{il|Despair}})
* {{sl|id=GluttonyOfElements}} skill from {{il|Blood of Corruption}}
* {{stl|Divinity}} buff from {{il|Garb of the Ephemeral}}
* [[Synthesised item|Synthesised]] shields with the {{ml|SynthesisImplicitImmuneToCursesCorruptedItem1}} synthesis implicit modifier

===Unaffected by curses===
"Unaffected by Curses" is distinct from curse immunity in that you can still be considered cursed for the purposes of modifiers like {{il|Self-Flagellation}}. Additionally, it also nullifies the effects of marks as well as hexes, unlike [[Hexproof]]. 

This modifier can be obtained from items such as {{il|Atziri's Reflection}} and the {{il|Zealotry}} version of {{il|Sublime Vision}}.

===Hex Reflection===
'''Hex Reflection''' is an effect that causes Hexes inflicted on the defender to also apply to the attacker. It does not remove the Hex from the defender.

===Self-curse===
In certain situations, a player may want to inflict a curse on themself to turn the detrimental effects into possibly useful ones in combination with other modifiers or stats. In order to curse yourself, one of the following is required:

* Curse a target with a hex socketed in {{il|Shackles of the Wretched}}
* Toggle on a hex socketed in {{il|Rotblood Promise}}
* Enter a {{il|Summon Skitterbots|Skitterbot}}'s {{il|Profane Proxy}} curse aura while wearing {{il|The Arkhon's Tools}} 
* Inflict a hex on a monster with the [[Hex Reflection]]/[[Curse Reflection]] modifier (e.g. [[Atziri]])
* Kill or overwrite [[totem]]s while wearing {{il|Soul Mantle}} <sup>(Not a "real" self-curse method)</sup>

All of the above methods except {{il|Soul Mantle}} scale with {{c|mod|#% increased/reduced/more/less Effect of your Curses}}. All of the above methods scale with {{c|mod|#% reduced/less Effect of Curses on You}}. Enemies' own sources of {{c|mod|#% reduced Effect of Curses on You}} do not affect reflected/self-inflicted curses. Increased effect of curses on you can be obtained by [[Reflecting Mist|Reflecting]] a ring with {{c|crafted|#% reduced Effect of Curses on you}}, and/or equipping a {{il|Penumbra Ring}} in the right ring slot.
 
{{il|Temporal Chains}} is the most common curse to curse yourself with. Reduced expiration rate of effects can be used to act as an effective more multiplier for duration effects on you, such as {{il|Immortal Call}}, or {{il|Boneshatter}} or {{il|Headhunter}} buff stacks. Temporal Chains' downside (reduced [[action speed]]) can be countered with increased action speed stats, or completely negated by {{c|mod|Action Speed cannot be modified to below base value}} (e.g. {{il|Kaom's Roots}}, [[Juggernaut]]'s {{psl|Unstoppable}}, {{il|The Balance of Terror}}, or an {{il|Animate Guardian}} with {{il|Garb of the Ephemeral}}) or {{c|mod|Your Action Speed is at least #% of base value}} (e.g. Trickster's {{psl|One Step Ahead}}, [[Scourge modifier]]s). Note that Temporal Chains has an innate 50% less Effect of Curse on players, making it harder to reach the cap.

{{il|Conductivity}} (and to a lesser extent, {{il|Elemental Weakness}}) may be used to achieve the -200% [[resistance]] cap for {{il|Doryani's Prototype}}. {{il|Replica Nebulis}} no longer benefits from self-cursing as it only requires 15%-20% resistance under the maximum to cap its effects (lower with certain [[heist enchantment]]s), which can easily be achieved through just equipment.

{{il|Self-Flagellation}} grants increased damage per curse on you; this works especially well with {{il|Soul Mantle}}.

{{il|Coward's Chains}}, {{il|Coward's Legacy}}, and {{il|Chains of Emancipation}} can also inflict curses on you, but these are not considered sources of self-cursing as they do not scale with your own curse effect.

==Gems==
===Skill gems===
There are {{Drop enabled gem count|where=skill_gems.gem_tags HOLDS "Curse" AND items.class_id="Active Skill Gem"}} curse [[skill gem]]s usable by players. When a player or monster is cursed, a curse icon will appear over their heads; the icon is the same as depicted on the skill icon. The [[Silence]] curse is used by monsters only.

A list of [[skill gem]]s with the [[:Category:Curse (gem tag)|Curse]] [[gem tag]]

}}

===Other===
* {{sl|id=Pacify}} (from {{il|The Queller of Minds}})
* {{sl|id=PenanceMark}} (from {{il|The Hateful Accuser}})
* {{stl|Silence}} is an enemy-exclusive hex that disables [[spell]]s and [[Warcry|warcries]]. It cannot be normally used by players, and can only be applied to enemies by stealing a [[monster modifier]] that applies random curses to an enemy, using a [[minion]] which can apply random curses, obtaining {{c|torment|Blasphemer's Touch}} using {{il|Fairgraves' Tricorne}}, obtaining {{c|torment|Blasphemer's Grip}} using {{psl|Speaker of the Dead}}, or by reflecting an enemy's Silence curse.

==Unique items==
The following [[unique items]] affects curses, hexes and/or marks:
{{Drop enabled unique item table
|tables = item_stats
|join = item_stats._pageName=items._pageName
|where = 
    ((item_stats.id LIKE "%curse%" AND item_stats.id NOT LIKE "%non\_curse\_aura%")
OR item_stats.id LIKE "%mark_skill%"
OR item_stats.id LIKE "%hexes%")
OR items.name = "Cinderswallow Urn"
|large=1
|level=1
|stat=1
|stat_column1_header=+# curse
|stat_column1_stat_format=add
|stat_column1_stat1_id=number_of_additional_curses_allowed
}}

==Passive skills==
There are [[passive skill]]s that grant curse bonuses.

===Radius for curses===
These passive skills grant increased [[area of effect]] radius for curses.
{{Query base passive skills
|where=
  passive_skill_stats.id = "curse_area_of_effect_+%"
}}

===Cast speed for curses===
These passive skills grant increased [[cast speed]] for curses.
{{Query base passive skills
|where=
  passive_skill_stats.id = "curse_cast_speed_+%"
}}

===Duration for curses===
These passive skills grant increased [[duration]] for curses.
{{Query base passive skills
|where=
  passive_skill_stats.id = "base_curse_duration_+%"
}}

===Effectiveness of curses===
These passive skills grant increased effect magnitude for curses.
{{Query base passive skills
|where=
  passive_skill_stats.id = "curse_effect_+%"
}}

===Additional curses===
These passive skill raise the active curse limit by one.
{{Query base passive skills
|where=
  passive_skill_stats.id = "number_of_additional_curses_allowed"
}}

===Reduced effect of curses on you===
These passive skills reduce the effect of curses on you
{{Query base passive skills
|where=
  passive_skill_stats.id like "%curse%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id = "curse_effect_on_self_+%"
}}

===Miscellaneous===
Curse passives that do not fit into other categories:
{{Query base passive skills
|where=
  passive_skill_stats.id like "%curse%" AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%non_curse%"
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT IN ("curse_area_of_effect_+%", "curse_cast_speed_+%", "base_curse_duration_+%", "curse_effect_+%", "number_of_additional_curses_allowed", "non_curse_aura_effect_+%", "curse_effect_on_self_+%")
  AND passive_skill_stats.id NOT LIKE "%cursed_treasure%"
}}

==Version history{{anchor|Doom}}==
Doom was a mechanic that interacted with [[Hex]]es between [[version 3.12.0]] and [[version 3.20.0]]. If a Hex curse was self-cast (e.g. not triggered or a curse aura), that instance of the Hex would gain a fixed amount of a counter known as "Doom" over time up to a maximum (30 by default). Hexes gained 1% increased Effect of that curse per count of Doom. Each instance of a Hex counted Doom independently, and re-casting the Hex would reset the Doom counter to 0. After the [[version 3.20.0]] curse rework, Hexes and certain Curse-related skills and items no longer use the Doom mechanic, but received buffs/reworks and had their penalties against various Unique monsters removed to compensate.

{{Version history table header}}
{{Version history table row|3.20.0|
* The Doom mechanic on Hexes has been removed.
* [[Pinnacle boss]]es, Map bosses, [[Incursion]] architects, [[Incursion_room#Architects|Betrayal]] targets, [[Breachlord]]s and others no longer have 33% or 66% less effect of curses on them respectively. 
}}
{{Version history table row|3.15.2|
* Monsters that cast Curses now have global cooldowns to prevent multiple of the same monster repeatedly cursing players.
}}
{{Version history table row|3.15.0f|
* Map Curse modifiers no longer have increased effect.
}}
{{Version history table row|3.15.0|
* The {{ml|FlaskCurseImmunity1}} <!-- "of Warding" --> Flask Suffix no longer grants Immunity to Curses during Flask effect.
}}
{{Version history table row|3.13.1e|
* Clarified that Hexes applied as Auras with Blasphemy Support do not gain Doom.
}}
{{Version history table row|3.12.0|
* All curse skills have been reworked and are now divided into two categories: Hexes and Marks.
** Hexes apply a curse in an area and, when manually cast, apply an amount of Doom per second to cursed enemies up to a maximum. Doom increases the effect of the afflicted curse and stacks additively with modifiers to increased Curse effect.
** Marks apply to a single targeted enemy, and only one enemy can be marked by you at a given time. Monster rarity no longer affects the efficacy of Marks. Monsters deep in the [[Azurite Mine]] (Delve) also no longer reduce the efficacy of Marks on them.
** Additions to the number of curses you can inflict on enemies apply cumulatively to both Hexes and Marks, but do not modify the number of enemies you can have Marked at any given time. Thus, you can have an enemy that is affected by both a Mark and a Hex, but you can't Mark an enemy with two Marks, nor can you Mark two different enemies.
** Items and enemies which previously reflected Curses will now only reflect Hexes.
}}
{{Version history table row|3.11.0|
* Added several new Curse- and [[Aura]]-centric notables.
}}
{{Version history table row|3.6.0|
* Bosses which previously had 60% or 80% less effect of curses on them now have 33% or 66% less effect of curses on them respectively. This includes map bosses, Incursion architects, Betrayal targets, Breachlords, Shaper, Elder and others.
* Modifiers which previously affected the [[Cast Speed]] and [[Duration]] of Curses now instead affect Curse Skills (including the Curses and {{il|Bane}}).
}}
{{Version history table row|2.4.0|
* [[Boss]]es that had a reduced effect of curses on them now have a multiplier rather than a reduction. Over time, more and more curse effect has been made available to players. With the boss curse effect reduction being additive, the increased curse effect available to players overwhelmed it. {{il|Temporal Chains}} and {{il|Enfeeble}} arguably still trivialise most bosses.
}}
{{Version history table row|2.0.0|
* [[Monster]]s that cast curses which lower player resistances should now do so less frequently. The curses now lower resistances less in Normal and Cruel [[Difficulty|difficulties]].
* [[Rogue Exile]]s no longer reduce the effect of player curses cast on them.
* [[Map]] bosses, meanwhile, reduce the effect of player curses cast on them even more than before.
}}
{{Version history table row|1.0.0|
Map Bosses now have 60% reduced curse effect (up from 50%).
Act bosses now have 70% reduced curse effect (up from 40%).
Rogue Exiles now have 50% reduced curse effect (up from 0%).
}}
{{Version history table row|0.9.2d|
Curse durations have been increased by 2 seconds at all levels.
}}
{{Version history table row|0.9.2b|
Fixed the way that the length of curses are described, to be clearer.
}}
{{Version history table end}}
